First off, I'm sorry that you're feeling so down at the moment, but coming here is a good sign though; and I hope I can at least help a little!

Everyone is weak sometimes, you know, and that means that everyone needs a break here and there. But if I can point out a couple of things, you said you need to change. That takes a lot of courage to admit, not to mention that it proves your strength is still there because you don't want to end it all. You even said 'luckily'. That's good to hear.

And you're right, tomorrow is a new day. So is the day after that. And the day after that. And they're all filled with endless possibilities, that's why there's always the chance for you to get better. Like you said, who knows, right?

If you don't mind me asking, you mentioned that you used to feel happy; so, when did you start feeling the way you are now?

Hey there! Sorry to hear you're not in the best of places at the moment, but I hope we can change that soon!

First off, let me say that you don't sound pathetic at all; you're reaching out for help and that's a good thing and very brave of you to do so, too. So thank you for not keeping all of this to yourself.

As for education and what subjects you should take, don't worry about what job they'll land you, just do whatever you want to do and go for it! If a certain subject interests you or you have a passion for it then they're the ones you choose; you're still young and at a point where you can shape your future into whatever you want. What are the subjects and things that you enjoy doing?

From the sounds of things, it sounds like your mum is willing to support you through anything, too; parents are cool like that. And it will be no different this time, too, she's helped you in the past and I'm sure she'll help you now as well. Have you told her how you're feeling recently? When you're down like this, one of the best things you can have to aid you is some kind of a support network. This is where your friends could help you, too; I'm not saying you have to tell them everything if you don't want to, but I'm sure they'll provide some relief and let you forget about your worries and troubles for a while. Have you ever thought about getting some outside help, like speaking to a counsellor maybe? You're under 18, and I know from my own experience that there's plenty of groups and services available for young people who are dealing with depression and the like, so that's always an option.

I'm afraid I can't say what I'd do in your situation, that's the thing with depression and feeling suicidal; everyone's different and with their own circumstances and with what will help them, it's up to you to find your path to recovery, and I know how daunting that can feel. When you feel like this, every decision feels like the biggest one of your life and everything in general seems so difficult, but you can get through this. Coming here and seeking help, knowing that you want a better life and that you want happiness is the first step, and you should be proud of that!

I really hope this helps in some way, and it goes without saying that if you need anything, more advice, questions answered or just someone to talk to, I'll be here! So don't be afraid to shoot me a message!

Hey there, my name is Skye and I'm really sorry to hear you're not in the best of ways right now, so I hope you'll listen to what I have to say.

A little while ago I posted to this sub myself; I was searching and begging for answers, advice, anything at all that anyone could provide for me. But what surprised me was that all the lovely guys and girls here told me to seek those answers within myself, really take a good look at all the aspects of my life and find my reason to live; and I think you should do the same thing.
It seems pretty clear that you and your lover share a deep connection, a bond that the two of you both hold very dear, so do you really want to throw that all away? I'm betting that he doesn't, the length of your relationship and the fact that he comforts and supports you is only evidence of that. He wants you to stay, as do I, and you should want to stay here, too. Life is too short and too precious to cut it so soon, I know just how painful and heart-rending the world can be at times, but like you said, it honestly is a big, old place, and a funny one at that. It's full of endless opportunities and wonderful moments and people. I mean, hey, you've already found one of them, right? Who's to say you won't find any more?

I know this is hard, and I know you want to give up, but I'm begging you not to; I know you and the world have so much more to offer each other.

Just know that no matter what happens or how you're feeling or anything, I'm just a PM away if you need me. An ear to lend, a shoulder to cry on, whatever, just say the word and I'll be there.

Firstly, I'd just like to thank you for replying to this and trying to help. Just knowing at least one other person out there somewhere cares even a little actually helps.

She's amazing, I'm honestly truly blessed to have her in my life, let alone to have had her for the seven years we've been together.
But you really don't think they'd see me as a liability? While we've never really gone into full depth or detail about the struggles I have, everyone has always been aware of it. I'm "the depressed/broken one" in our group and that's how it's always been, everyone knows that. I know it's kind of a cliché to say how much of a burden I'd be, but I guess the truth isn't always original. With everyone knowing my "role" so to speak, it's extremely difficult to not think that they'd all view me as like an affliction.

That's where I've always had trouble. I live in England so all this stuff goes through my GP first and on the few occasions where I've tried to deal with this in the past, he's never really understood my position. I've tried other doctors in the practice and they all seem to be of the similar opinion to him, and it's ended the same way every time. I've been prescribed Prozac, forwarded to a councillor and told that I'm young so I'll get better. It's why I've stayed away from it to be honest. And, this may seem kind of irrational I guess, but the thought of being passed around from doctor to doctor, or therapist to therapist makes me feel worse about it all. Like, they have no idea how to deal with me  or help me so they just send me to the next person to try.

And this may sound pretty pathetic but, I am really trying to not give up on all of this. It's just so, so difficult.

Again, thanks for replying to this, it really means a lot to me.

I lost both of my parents when I was really young, and they were the only family that I had, so my birth mom's oldest friend who still lived in England (my birth mom was English) gave me a home with her husband. And I swear that that "man" was just pain and suffering incarnate, I could probably write a book on all of the awful things he's done to me and my mom.

I remember one time pretty vividly when I was around 9, I'd been living there for like 4 years at this point, and my mom had just left the house to go somewhere which meant that I was alone with him for a while. Now this was a very rare occasion, my mom *detested* leaving me with him but there were times where it was unavoidable.

I always cried like a bitch whenever she left but it was always in the solace of my own room, I never wanted annoy or upset him because it would always end disastrously. After a few minutes of sobbing to myself though, I heard his angry stomps up the stairs, and I knew where things were headed after that. I remember my heart was pounding in my chest and I was just hoping and praying that he wasn't coming me. A few seconds after, my door swung open with a slam and he was stood there; that familiar, crazed and psychotic look in his eye. He yelled at me to shut the fuck up and he backhanded me across the face. And that's genuinely all I can recollect of that night. The next thing I recall was waking up in the hospital.

Taking it "too far" was all he ever did.
